'''Armed conflicts and attacks''' 
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Kryvyi Rih strikes (2022–present)|Kryvyi Rih strikes]]
***Four people are killed and 14 others are injured in a [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian]] [[ballistic missile]] strike on [[Kryvyi Rih]], [[Ukraine]], according to the [[Governor of Dnipropetrovsk Oblast]] [[Serhiy Lysak]]. [https://www.euronews.com/my-europe/2025/01/18/four-killed-in-russian-air-strike-on-kryvyi-rih-as-zelenskyy-bemoans-lack-of-air-defences (Euronews)]
**[[Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure (2022–present)|Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure]]
***At least four people are killed in Russian missile and [[Drone warfare|drone attacks]] on [[Kyiv]], Ukraine. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/1/18/russian-attacks-on-centre-of-kyiv-leave-four-dead (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]]
**[[Gaza war]]
***The [[Government of Israel]] approves the proposed [[January 2025 Gaza war ceasefire|Gaza ceasefire agreement]], which had previously been approved by the [[Security Cabinet of Israel]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/2025/01/18/middleeast/israel-approves-ceasefire-hostage-deal-intl-hnk/index.html?iid=cnn_buildContentRecirc_end_recirc (CNN)]
**A [[Palestinian]] man from [[Tulkarm]] in the [[West Bank]] stabs and seriously injures a man in central [[Tel Aviv]] after illegally entering [[Israel]]. An armed civilian subsequently shoots and kills the perpetrator. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/man-seriously-hurt-in-tel-aviv-stabbing-palestinian-terrorist-shot-dead/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
*[[2025 assassination of Iranian Supreme Court judges]]
**Two judges are killed and a third judge and a bodyguard are injured in a mass shooting at the [[Supreme Court of Iran]] in [[Tehran]], [[Iran]]. The perpetrator subsequently [[murder–suicide|kills himself]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/iran-two-judges-shot-dead-outside-supreme-court-in-tehran/a-71335185 (DW)]
*[[Ghana Army|Ghanian soldiers]] open fire on [[illegal mining|illegal miners]] at a [[Gold mining|gold mine]] in [[Ashanti Region]], killing seven people. [[President of Ghana|Ghanian president]] [[John Mahama]] calls for an investigation into the incident. [https://apnews.com/article/ghana-illegal-gold-mining-soldiers-anglogold-ashanti-abd602d2574d19281550244dc8a622cd (AP)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2025 Suleja fuel tanker explosion]]
**At least 86 people are killed and several others are injured when a [[Tank truck|fuel tanker]] overturns on a highway in [[Suleja]], [[Niger (state)|Niger State]], [[Nigeria]], and later explodes when people gather to collect the spilled fuel. [https://www.vanguardngr.com/2025/01/death-toll-in-niger-petrol-tanker-explosion-now-70/ (Vanguard)] [https://www.straitstimes.com/world/fuel-tanker-truck-blast-kills-at-least-60-in-nigeria (The Straits Times)]
*Ten people are injured, including two seriously, when a [[chairlift]] collapses at the [[Astún]] [[ski resort]] in [[Aragon]], [[Spain]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/ckgydwvkv1do (BBC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2023–2024 mpox epidemic]]
**[[Azerbaijan]]'s [[Ministry of Healthcare (Azerbaijan)|Ministry of Healthcare]] reports the country's first case of [[mpox]] in a 22-year-old patient who had recently travelled abroad. [https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/first-mpox-case-detected-azerbaijan-interfax-reports-2025-01-18/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Internet censorship in the United States]]
**[[Apple Inc.|Apple]] and [[Google]] remove apps by the [[China|Chinese]] company [[ByteDance]], including [[TikTok]], [[Lemon8]], and [[CapCut]], from their app stores in the [[United States]] to comply with the [[Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act]]. [https://www.reuters.com/technology/tiktok-faces-us-ban-deadline-users-brace-fallout-2025-01-18/ (Reuters)] [https://www.cnbc.com/2025/01/18/apple-google-remove-tiktok-from-stores-as-app-halts-service-in-us.html (CNBC)]
